stem:
A small wooden block (cuboid) of mass *m* floats in water, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The top face of the block is horizontal and has area *A*. The density of the water is *ρ*.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the names of the two forces acting on the block when it is stationary.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The block is now displaced downwards as shown in Fig. 3.2 so that the surface of the water is higher up the block.

[[fig:f2]]

State and explain the direction of the resultant force acting on the wooden block in this position.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The block in (b) is now released so that it oscillates vertically.

The resultant force *F* acting on the block is given by

*F* = −*Aρgx*

where *g* is the gravitational field strength and *x* is the vertical displacement of the block from the equilibrium position.
parts.text: Explain why the oscillations of the block are simple harmonic.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Show that the angular frequency *ω* of the oscillations is given by

$ω = \sqrt{\frac{Aρg}{m}}$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead:
The block is now placed in a liquid with a greater density. The block is displaced and released so that it oscillates vertically. The variation with displacement *x* of the acceleration *a* of the block is measured for the first half oscillation, as shown in Fig. 3.3.

[[fig:f3]]
parts.text: Explain why the maximum negative displacement of the block is not equal to its maximum positive displacement.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The mass of the block is 0.57 kg.

Use Fig. 3.3 to determine the decrease Δ*E* in energy of the oscillation for the first half oscillation.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: A wooden block of mass m floats partly submerged in water of density ρ.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.2
figures.alt: A block is shown displaced downwards, with the new water surface above the dashed line marking the original water surface.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.3
figures.alt: A graph of acceleration a against displacement x shows a straight line sloping downwards from positive acceleration at negative displacement to negative acceleration at positive displacement.
